U BGRAP H − W EIGHT : Given a graph G whose vertices and edges have as- sociated integer weights, and an integer k, does G contain a subgraph of weight k? (Define the weight of a graph to be the sum of the weights of the vertices and edges of that graph.)  prove this is NP-Complete

message.content:
The problem is clearly defined for us.

We can easily verify any proposed solution quickly here.

Therefore, the problem belongs to the class NP now.

To prove hardness we reduce from Subset Sum.

Given a set of integers $S = \{w_1, ..., w_n\}$ and target $K$, construct graph G.

For each integer $w_i$, create a vertex $v_i$ with weight $w_i$.

Add no edges between any of these isolated vertices in G.

Set the desired subgraph weight exactly equal to the target K.

A subset of vertices has total weight K if and only if Subset Sum is yes.

This reduction takes polynomial time because constructing G is trivial linear work.

Thus, Subgraph Weight is NP-hard since Subset Sum reduces to it.

Combining membership in NP with NP-hardness proves Subgraph Weight is NP-Complete.
